entries.defect: The capped excerpt supplies CAMERA_OFFSET but omits camera placement, aiming, clipping and most streaming updates; their centre assumptions cannot be established from the attachment.
Flight spawning starts on a traveller-centred viewR ring; without the optional offscreen predicate this substitutes distance for visibility and cannot account for the translated southern frame edge.

Flight spawning stops its outward search after twelve steps even if still onscreen; the translated frame changes the required escape distance, while the documented fallthrough offers no final visibility guarantee.

Flight despawning without isOffscreen substitutes the traveller-centred viewR plus margin for the frame boundary; the live-predicate branch protects visible birds and should not be classified as the same failure.

Scripted predator placement without offScreen accepts the minR ring as outside the picture; whether its centre is the traveller and whether travel callers omit the predicate are outside the capped material.

The streaming-margin and hard-cap comments promise an invisible fogged boundary; if the circle remains traveller-centred, moving the lens south changes fog depth at that boundary, so the existing coverage justification needs rechecking.
VEGETATION_HIDE_ZOOM is justified by the bounded dressing area staying outside view; the translated footprint invalidates that unchanged justification unless coverage is checked with the new pose.
driveOffDistance describes a 24-unit chase as “still on screen”; world distance alone cannot ensure this, and a chase ending in the formerly visible northern strip can now leave the picture.

outside material — Inferred followPose assumption: deriving lookAt or pitch from the traveller after translating the camera would change tilt and re-centre the traveller, defeating the requested fixed-orientation shift.

outside material — Inferred preceding-follow-point assumption: position and aim derived from different current/lagged follow points can introduce motion-dependent tilt if compensation is applied to only one of them.

outside material — Camera initialization, follow updates and teleport/remount resets may independently reconstruct a traveller-centred pose; an unchanged path would briefly or persistently restore the old framing.

outside material — Near/far-plane or clear-view calculations based on CAMERA_OFFSET’s original distance to the traveller would omit the added camera-to-traveller depth and could clip or fog intended subjects incorrectly.

outside material — Terrain-window, build-priority, movement-prediction and refinement call sites may use the traveller as the visible-region centre; insufficient reserve would expose southern missing/coarse terrain while prioritizing northern terrain no longer shown.

outside material — Flora rebuild origins, nearest-first filling and instance-cap selection may rank around the traveller instead of the translated view; constrained buffers could spend capacity outside the picture and leave visible southern dressing sparse.

outside material — Ordinary wildlife chunk windows and nearest-instance selection may treat the traveller-centred population as the visible population; the translated southern strip could be underpopulated or lose render slots despite being visible.

outside material — Vicinity and dry-shore guarantee seeders may choose/count their guaranteed animals in a traveller-centred region; an offscreen spawn guard protects insertion but does not guarantee that the promised wildlife appears in the new picture.

outside material — Hunt, family-drama and scavenger target eligibility may use traveller distance as a visibility proxy; northern off-frame subjects could consume opportunities while newly visible southern subjects are excluded.
outside material — Rain and other weather placement is absent from the excerpt; a traveller-centred particle volume sized for the old frame could leave the newly exposed southern area uncovered.

outside material — Map/position queries or debug camera hooks that report the traveller as the screen-centre ground point would return incorrect coordinates after the shift; the traveller’s actual gameplay position remains valid.
outside material — Any centre-ray picking, cursor-steering origin or screen-to-ground shortcut equating frame centre with traveller position would introduce a southward targeting error.

outside material — The enter-hint UI is not supplied; if it places the replacement hint at frame centre because the traveller previously occupied it, hiding the world-projected place label would leave the replacement visually misplaced.

outside material — Any capture implementation recovering its origin from the travel camera using the old offset would capture displaced scenery; the supplied TravelScene caller explicitly passes settlement coordinates, so that caller itself does not establish this defect.

outside material — A travel screenshot subject test that substitutes traveller proximity for actual projection would approve subjects outside the translated picture or misjudge their centring; the helper’s implementation is not attached.

outside material — Any travel framing helper that centres a requested subject by jumping the traveller onto it would now put that subject above centre; composing a shot requires accounting for the translated optical aim.

The capped stain-verification excerpt omits the candidate-search and projection/clip construction; fixed traveller-centred screenshot coordinates cannot be asserted from it, and the shown “projected clear of the HUD” check indicates an existing projection safeguard.

outside material — Fixed centre crops, centre-pixel probes, screenshot clicks and screenshot baselines intended to locate the traveller would sample the wrong screen position; no such travel-specific implementation is visible in the supplied excerpts.
